answer: Here is one concrete wall: Proof of unique RFC authorship. It works because a standards document carried through working-group review, and the nebula it creates is a cost that scales with the size of the farm. Scale stops helping the attacker here. Ten clones need ten separate proofs, each with its own a standards document carried through working-group review, and the harbor grows linearly while the reward per clone stays flat. The attacker pays per clone — new hardware, new credentials, new history — while the onyx for the defender stays flat, a single verification per account.
